response.sql: WITH mt AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name, CAST(SUM(t.Bytes) AS REAL) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track t JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.Name), avg_all AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM mt) SELECT AVG(mt.rate) AS avg_rate, AVG(mt.track_count) AS avg_track_count, AVG(mt.rate - avg_all.avg_rate) AS avg_excess FROM mt CROSS JOIN avg_all WHERE mt.rate > avg_all.avg_rate

assumptions.assumption: Media types are grouped by name via an inner join to MediaType, so only tracks with a matching media type are counted. Media types with no tracks are excluded. Media types sharing a name are merged.

Track count is COUNT(*) of tracks per media type. Bytes may be NULL, so SUM(Bytes) ignores those rows while SUM(Milliseconds) includes them. This means the rate is not strictly bytes per millisecond over the same tracks.
The rate is computed as a real number, not integer division, and no rounding is applied.
